posts.name: broccoli
posts.cooked:
Reckless:

The issue of The Sentinels surviving the game was a HUGE deal in playtesting. Over the various playtest builds I noticed a significant increase in their ability to remain standing.

I think they'll be considered quite an impressive team.

This.  They're very powerful, but very vulnerable to AE.  I tend to think of them as a more resilient, less "broken if left alone" version of Unity's bots.  My favorite part about them is that they require very little build up.  They have a few Ongoings and 1 Equipment, but otherwise, they're about as powerful on turn 1 as on turn 20 (and trust me, they're pretty powerful on turn 1).

posts.name: McBehrer
posts.cooked: There are actually 2 un-incap cards; one ONLY does that, so it's a dud if none of them are dead. The other also heals all hero targets, but because resurrecting someone is so powerful it might as well be a dud. Also, Mainstay is a tanking BEAST. Not quite like the Scholar, but he can maintain a permanent DR2 (DR1 on ALL HERO TARGETS) plus additional if he gets extra powers (Argent Adept, Greatest Legacy, etc.) and an optionally triggered Alchemical Redirection that you can maintain for multiple turns. They are SURPRISINGLY survivable. Not to mention the fact that Medico is the best healer in the game.

posts.name: broccoli
posts.cooked:
McBehrer:

(DR1 on ALL HERO TARGETS)

That's all YOUR hero targets.  Thus all hero targets of the player playing The Sentinels, thus on all Sentinels.

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
Sentinels are nasty.

Yes they have low health and things can get dicey. But thats their downside. They have an upside equally as impressive. Consider most heros Power curve over time, they all need a little setup time to get going. A few rounds to get engines rolling. Sentinels are at the top of their power curve from their first turn. Their one shots are awesome, among the best in the game. They have the ability to dig in their deck quickly, play multiple cards/powers, tons of damage...these guys got serious power to balance out.

posts.name: lynkfox
posts.cooked:
Rules question time

 

Restorative Burst

If Dr Medico is active, you may flip one of your incapacitated heroes and restory it to 3hp. Each hero regains 1 hp.

 

Second Chance

Flip one of your character cards from its incapacitated side to its active side. Restore it to 6 hp.

 

 

The different wording (of Character cards vrs heroes) throws me a little - Does anyone think that it can be used on non Sentinel cards? I don't think so because it says 'Your'  and there is no card draw or anything to help get an incapped hero back into the game. 

 

But the wording difference makes me sigh a little, my desire for well templated wording.

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked: There is a team wide heal on Burst that hits all heros. Think Fanatic. The wording seems clear to me as to what is supposed to happen.

posts.name: BrotherDusk
posts.cooked:
A question about how the Mini-Nemisis fit into the vengeance villian decks for someone who has the game or playtested:

Do the Mini nemisis cards generally do things that are in line with the particular villian deck they fit within or would you say they have more random effects that are in line with the character on the card?  For instance, are the mini-nemisis cards in Friction's deck very focused on playing multiple cards quickly like I imagine her own cards are, or do they do things totally unrelated to her theme?  Are Fright Train's mini nemisis cards preoccupied with big damage?

Thanks in advance!

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
The mini-nemmys have effects and added effects that are more in-line thematically with who their acctual hero nemmy is. 

For instance, Calypso, a water spirit like woman who is a nemmy of Ra, she will reduce fire damage if Ra is in play

posts.name: broccoli
posts.cooked: Not really, no.  That said, 2 of the Nemeses in Ermine's deck destroy ongoings or environment cards, and he deck is mostly about that kind of manipulation.  All the nemeses DO interact with their Nemeses however.  I haven't tried to do any "math" to see if there's some correlation there, like the nemeses in Ermine's deck are all likely to oppose Wraith or something similar.  I do know that both Fixer's and Expatriette's nemeses are in Baron Blade's deck, but the other 2 Dark Watch members are NOT.  I feel confident that there is SOME logic to whose decks they're in, but I haven't grokked it yet.
